  1. Take the application form for the post of Contractual / Temporary Staff Nurse, printed in the notice under the National Health Mission – Tamil Nadu and the District Health Society, Thiruvarur heading.
  2. Enter the details asked: name, father's name, date of birth, age, gender, qualification, institution, council registration number, addresses, Aadhar number, phone number, email ID (if available) and community.

  5. Affix a passport size photograph and sign the declaration with place and date.
  6. Attach the certificates that support the details given in the form.
  7. Send the application to: The Executive Secretary, District Health Society and District Health Office, Old Government Hospital Campus, Netty Velaikkarar Street, Thiruvarur-610001.

The Sálim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History (SACON), South India Centre of Wildlife Institute of India under the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change, Government of India, is engaging research personnel (Indian Nationals only) on a purely temporary basis for five Project Associate-I and Project Associate-II positions in three projects. Duration is one year (likely to be extended), and pay runs from Rs. 30,000 + HRA to Rs. 42,000 + HRA a month depending on the post and NET/GATE status. An M.Sc. or equivalent with a minimum of 55% marks in life sciences or environmental sciences is the essential qualification. Apply online at https://wii-saconrp.in/ by 5:00 PM on 7 December 2026.

About SACON

SACON is the South India Centre of the Wildlife Institute of India, located at Moongilpallam, Anaikatty (PO), Coimbatore – 641 108, Tamil Nadu. The notice is issued by the Nodal Officer, Recruitment and Placement Cell, WII-SACON. These posts are in SACON's own research projects and are a government institute's temporary project engagements, not regular posts.

Vacancy Details

SACON has printed one position each for three of the posts and two for Project Associate-I in Project 3, which makes 5 positions in total. The notice prints no category-wise break-up.

Ref.PostProjectVacancies
1(a)Project Associate-IConservation of the Nicobar Megapode [PI - Dr. Manchi Shirish S.]1

Only Indian Nationals may apply. Candidates must hold all the essential qualifications, with originals of supporting documents, as on the date of the application deadline. The upper age limit for every post is 35 years as on 07-12-2026.

Project Associate-I (1(a) and 3(b))Post-Graduate degree (M.Sc.) or its equivalent with a minimum of 55% marks in life sciences or environmental sciences from a recognized university.
Project Associate-II (Molecular Biology) (2(a))Post-Graduate degree (M.Sc.) or its equivalent with a minimum of 55% marks in life sciences from a recognized university, AND two years of post-PG research experience in relevant scientific projects and activities.
Project Associate-II (3(a))Post-Graduate degree (M.Sc.) or its equivalent with a minimum of 55% marks in life sciences or environmental sciences from a recognized university, AND two years of post-PG research experience in relevant scientific projects and activities.

Accepted disciplines as printed. Project Associate-I (1(a)): Zoology, Wildlife Biology, Wildlife Science, Forestry, Conservation Biology, Biodiversity Studies, Ecological Sciences, Environmental Studies or any other allied disciplines. Project Associate-I (3(b)) and Project Associate-II (3(a)): the same list, with "any allied disciplines" for 3(b). Project Associate-II (Molecular Biology): Zoology, Wildlife Science, Forestry, Conservation Biology, Biodiversity Studies, Ecological Sciences, Environmental Studies, Molecular Biology, Biotechnology, Microbiology or any other allied disciplines.

Project Associate-I – Project 1, post 1(a)

  • Interest in bird research and conservation.
  • Skill and experience in bird surveys and field ecology methods.
  • Willingness to reside in remote locations with challenging conditions and travel extensively by road and sea between the islands.
  • Prior exposure to field techniques for bird capture, handling and collection of biological samples for disease screening.
  • Familiarity with data analysis, including R programming and GIS tools.
  • Proficiency in English and Hindi (speaking, reading, and writing).

Project Associate-II (Molecular Biology) – Project 2, post 2(a)

  • Experience with molecular biology techniques, including RNA/DNA isolation, NGS library preparation, and developing pipelines for various NGS applications.
  • Experience with targeted RT-qPCR and NGS platforms.
  • Expertise in analysing mid/or whole genome data types.
  • Familiarity with wildlife population-level studies using molecular techniques.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and ability to contribute in a team-based environment.
  • Good written and oral communication skill.

Project Associate-II – Project 3, post 3(a)

  • Interest in studying avian ecology and conservation; skill in field identification of birds.
  • Prior experience in bird survey methods and sampling design.
  • Willingness to reside in remote locations with challenging conditions and travel extensively by road and sea between the islands.
  • Familiarity with basic data analysis and GIS tools.
  • Proficiency in English (speaking, reading, and writing) and Hindi (speaking).

Project Associate-I – Project 3, post 3(b)

  • Interest in studying avian ecology and conservation; skill in field identification of birds.
  • Familiarity with bird survey methods and sampling design.
  • Willingness to reside in remote locations with challenging conditions and travel extensively by road and sea between the islands.
  • Familiarity with basic data analysis and GIS tools.
  • Proficiency in English (speaking, reading, and writing) and Hindi (speaking).

Age Relaxation

The upper age limit may be relaxed as per Government of India norms: up to 5 years for SC/ST candidates and up to 3 years for OBC candidates.

Candidates should check the official notification for the discipline-specific eligibility of each post.

PostCSIR-UGC NET (Lectureship)/GATE qualifiedNon-NET/GATE qualified
Project Associate-I (1(a), 3(b))Rs.37,000 + HRARs. 30,000 + HRA
Project Associate-II (Molecular Biology) (2(a)) and Project Associate-II (3(a))Rs.42,000 + HRARs. 33,000 + HRA

Each post is for one year (likely to be extended) on a purely temporary basis. Selected candidates will be provided hostel accommodation at SACON as per availability. Other allowances and benefits to the research personnel will be admissible as per the rules.

SACON Recruitment 2026 Job Description

Project Associate-I – Project 1, post 1(a)

  • Conduct species population surveys and ecological studies in remote areas of Andaman and Nicobar Islands with limited resources and challenging field conditions.
  • Collect and analyze field data and contribute to preparation of reports.
  • Assist with conducting social surveys among local communities to understand their views on species conservation.
  • Work closely with the forest department and local communities to develop sustainable conservation/management plan.
  • Assist the Project Investigator and senior project staff in achieving project goals and other institutional activities.

Project Associate-II (Molecular Biology) – Project 2, post 2(a)

  • Collect biological samples from birds following ethical guidelines and standard protocols.
  • Undertake laboratory work and data analysis.
  • Maintain lab diary and analytical records.
  • Assist the PI in achieving project goals and other institutional activities.

Project Associate-II – Project 3, post 3(a)

  • Conduct field studies on endemic and cavity-nesting birds in remote areas of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
  • Collect and analyze field data and assist in drafting project reports.
  • Work closely with the forest department and local communities to develop sustainable conservation/management plan.
  • Assist the Project Investigator and senior project staff in achieving project goals and other institutional activities.

Project Associate-I – Project 3, post 3(b)

  • Conduct field studies on endemic and cavity-nesting birds in remote areas of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
  • Collect and analyze field data and contribute to preparation of project reports.
  • Work closely with the forest department and local communities to develop sustainable conservation/management plan.
  • Assist the Project Investigator and senior project staff in achieving project goals and other institutional activities.

How to Apply for SACON Recruitment 2026

  1. Fill in and submit the Application Form through SACON's Online Application Portal (https://wii-saconrp.in/) by 5:00 PM on 07 December 2026.
  2. Submit the form online only, with self-attested scanned PDF copies of all supporting documents uploaded on the portal. The notice says not to send hard copies of application forms and attachments.
  3. Pay the fee through the online payment gateway at the Application Portal: Rs. 500/- for General, or Rs.100/- Application Processing Fee for SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD.
  4. OBC candidates should upload a valid OBC certificate endorsed by the Government of India and issued by competent authorities, and should not submit other certificates in its place.
  5. To apply for more than one position (maximum two), submit separate sets of applications and supporting documents, with the fee paid separately for each position.
  6. For technical issues or queries, write to [email protected] or call the landline 0422-2203114 or mobile 91593 94160.

Documents named in the notice

  • Copies of certificates, mark lists and testimonials of essential and desirable qualifications.
  • Proof of research/work experience, date of birth, community and extracurricular activities.
  • Valid OBC certificate endorsed by the Government of India (OBC candidates).
  • At joining, if selected: originals of all documents for verification, the hard copy of the filled-in application form and self-attested true copies of all supporting documents.

Selection and Interview

Only shortlisted candidates will be invited for the Online Interview, through which the final selection is made. The exact date, time and online link will be intimated individually to shortlisted candidates by email. The notice does not describe the shortlisting criteria.

Important Instructions

  • Fees are non-refundable under any circumstances, and non-payment of fees leads to rejection of the application.
  • Canvassing in any form is liable to rejection of the candidature.
  • The Director, WII-SACON reserves the right to reject any application for incomplete information, no supporting documents, non-payment of prescribed fees, submission after the deadline, or any other reason.
  • A candidate can apply for a maximum of two positions only.
  • The duration of one year is "likely to be extended"; the notice states the posts are on a purely temporary basis.

NCrF stands for National Credit Framework, and the other five notices carry this label. The titles also separate "Honours" from "Honours with Research". If you are unsure which applies to you, check your enrolment details or ask your department.

Kadapa DCCB 2026 Marking Scheme and Score Calculation

Wrong answers carry a penalty in the Kadapa DCCB online exam. Scores are equated across sessions, and cut-offs are applied in two stages.

PostPenalty for Each Wrong Answer
Assistant Manager0.25 or 1/4th of the marks assigned to that question
Staff Assistant (Open)0.25 or 1/4th of the marks assigned to that question
Staff Assistant (In-Service PACS)0.25 marks
  • The number of questions answered correctly in each test is used to arrive at the Corrected Score, after the penalty for wrong answers is applied.
  • Corrected Scores are equated to allow for small differences in difficulty between tests held in different sessions. This gives the Equated Scores.
  • Test-wise scores and total scores are reported to two decimal places.
  • Cut-offs are applied in two stages: first on the scores in individual tests, then on the Total Score.

Kadapa DCCB Online Exam Instructions 2026

The handout explains how the online test works and lists the general instructions for the exam venue. The main points are below.

Kadapa DCCB Online Test Interface

Candidates answer each question on screen with a mouse click.

  • An answer is counted only if it is saved with "Save & Next" or "Mark for Review & Next". Questions marked "Answered and Marked for Review" are evaluated.
  • A countdown timer at the top right shows the time left. The exam ends on its own when the time runs out.
  • The question palette shows each question's status: not visited, not answered, answered, marked for review, or answered and marked for review.
  • Clicking a question number on the palette does not save the answer to the current question.
  • To deselect an answer, click the chosen option again or click Clear Response.
  • Sections appear on the top bar. After the last question of a section, "Save & Next" moves to the next section.
  • Candidates cannot "finally submit" before the full test time is over. They must not press any keyboard keys once the exam starts.
  • Doubts can be raised with the Test Administrator only before the test begins.

Kadapa DCCB Exam Day Instructions

Candidates must bring the call letter, an ID proof and a ball point pen to the venue.

  • The exam date, reporting time and venue address are given in the call letter. Late comers will not be allowed.
  • Bring the call letter with a recent passport-size photo pasted on it, a photocopy of the photo ID proof stapled to it, and the same ID proof in original.
  • Valid ID proofs: PAN Card, Passport, Permanent Driving License, Voter's Card, Bank Passbook with photograph, photo ID from a Gazetted Officer or People's Representative on official letterhead, College/University ID card, Aadhar/E-aadhar card, Employee ID or Bar Council ID card. Ration Card and Learner's Driving License are not accepted.
  • The name on the call letter must exactly match the name on the photo ID proof. Candidates who have changed their name must show the Gazette notification, marriage certificate or affidavit.
  • Calculators, books, notebooks, cell phones and other electronic devices are not allowed.
  • Biometric data (thumb impression) and a photograph will be taken before and after the exam. Fingers should be clean and dry, with no ink or mehndi.
  • A sheet of paper for rough work will be provided. It must be handed back to the Test Administrator before leaving.
  • Responses will be checked for similarity with other candidates' answers. Copying or unfair means may lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • Candidates should note "The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024".
